chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Sayf ibn Umayrah, from Muhammad ibn Humran, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When there occurred in the matter of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) what occurred, the angels cried out to Allah with weeping and said: "Is this to be done to al-Husayn, Your chosen one and the son of Your Prophet?" He said: So Allah established for them the shadow-image of al-Qa'im (peace be upon him) and said: "By this one I shall take revenge for this one."

key_terms.أَنْتَقِمُ: I shall take revenge, meaning divine retribution for the wrong committed
key_terms.الْبُكَاءِ: weeping, expressing sorrow over the tragedy
key_terms.الْحُسَيْنِ: al-Husayn (peace be upon him), the martyred grandson of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.الْقَائِمِ: al-Qa'im (peace be upon him), the one through whom vengeance will be taken
key_terms.الْمَلَائِكَةُ: the angels, who are described here as grieving and crying out
key_terms.صَفِيِّكَ: Your chosen one, indicating special nearness and distinction before Allah

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith connect the martyrdom of al-Husayn (عليه السلام) with al-Qa'im (عليه السلام) and divine vengeance?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts the heavenly response to the tragedy of al-Husayn (عليه السلام), describing the grief of the angels before Allah. It also links the future rising of al-Qa'im (عليه السلام) with divine vengeance for al-Husayn (عليه السلام), expressing a strong eschatological and theological connection between Karbala and ultimate justice.
